source_refs.note: Topic 1.8.3, printed pages 15-16: the reactions with chlorine, with Quick Check 1.4 as the self-check.

blocks.text: Chlorine reacts with both metals to give soluble salts. It reacts exothermically with sodium, a golden yellow flame is seen and the white solid sodium chloride is formed: 2Na(s) + Cl2(g) gives 2NaCl(s). Magnesium also reacts with chlorine to give the white solid magnesium chloride: Mg(s) + Cl2(g) gives MgCl2(s).

blocks.prompt: What is the nature of the oxides and hydroxides of sodium and magnesium, and what would you predict for calcium, a group 2 element, with water and oxygen?
blocks.explanation: The oxides and hydroxides of both are basic. Calcium, below magnesium in group 2, is more metallic and reactive, so it reacts with cold water more readily than magnesium to give calcium hydroxide and hydrogen, and burns in oxygen to give the basic oxide calcium oxide.

items: Chlorine gives white soluble chlorides with both metals: 2Na + Cl2 gives 2NaCl (golden flame, exothermic); Mg + Cl2 gives MgCl2.
